exposure: Systemic antibiotic exposure in the first 90 days
outcome: Incidence of physician-diagnosed infections (recurrent respiratory tract infections)
cohort: The study included 180 term infants who were enrolled at birth and followed until 12 months of age.
finding: Early-life antibiotic exposure induces persistent microbiome alterations that are independently associated with impaired linear growth and increased immune-mediated disease (recurrent respiratory tract infections and eczema) in the first year of life.
